name: Soft bottom (silty sand / mud)
role_for_lumpfish: Not used for nests; adults may cross it. Avoid in module footprint (organic-rich sediment also limits eelgrass, P25)
danish_cover_or_density: Common in fjords and deeper basins

name: Sand (0.06-2 mm, rippled)
role_for_lumpfish: Soft side of the hard/soft edge next to nests (R15); substrate for eelgrass. Eggs are not laid on sand (none of the readable sources report sand nests)
gaps: Edge rule rests on one nest

name: Sand/gravel/small stones 2-10 cm (class 2a-2b, <10% stones >10 cm)
role_for_lumpfish: Too small and mobile for nests; possible cobble apron base
needs: Stable only if stones >5-10 cm on exposed sites

name: Scattered stones >10 cm at 10-25% cover (class 3)
role_for_lumpfish: Reef margin; counts as reef only next to class 4
danish_cover_or_density: Reef boundary drawn where cover falls to 10%
measurable_from_open_data: Side-scan/ROV only; not in open grids

name: Stone reef: stones >10 cm at >25% cover (class 4, habitat 1170)
role_for_lumpfish: Nesting: eggs laid 'on stones and amongst Laminaria beds, but not on exposed rock'; nests 'around rocky areas and in crevices'
needs: Stable stones; restoration prefers rounded stones, then field stone, then quarry stone
danish_cover_or_density: Reefs mapped in Natura 2000 areas; no national total; stone fishing (4-7 m) depleted shallow reefs until 2009 ban
measurable_from_open_data: EMODnet 'rock and boulders'; MST 1170 mapping (download route unconfirmed)
gaps: Stone size actually used by nesting lumpfish not measured

name: Boulders with crevices (nest boulders)
role_for_lumpfish: Male guards eggs in crevice/rock depression; egg mass up to 26 x 10 x 10 cm; male fans eggs, deeper eggs develop slower (needs water exchange)
needs: Crevice open to water flow; overhang/concealment not a female-choice criterion in Newfoundland
danish_cover_or_density: Danish reef stones 'tens of cm to over 1 m' (Gilleleje)
measurable_from_open_data: Boulders >~1.6 m only, from 1 m lidar (intertidal) or multibeam
gaps: Boulder and crevice size are inferred (R03-R06)

name: Bedrock / chalk
role_for_lumpfish: Rocky shores used elsewhere; in Denmark only chalk (Stevns) and Bornholm. Chalk and shale are poor restoration material

name: Blue mussel bed (Mytilus edulis), biogenic reef
role_for_lumpfish: Listed 1170 subtype 'stable shallow reef dominated by Mytilus'; role for lumpfish unknown

name: Eelgrass (Zostera marina)
role_for_lumpfish: Shallow cover on sand landward of the reef; no source reports lumpfish juveniles using eelgrass
needs: Sand with organic matter <13%; depth limit ~0.74 x Secchi (P21, P25)

name: Sugar kelp (Saccharina latissima)
role_for_lumpfish: Mating 'on rocky shores, particularly in areas overgrown with kelp'; juveniles associated with kelp (Laminaria)
needs: Stable stones (needs >= ~10% hard stable substrate); large kelp can move stones <7-10 cm on exposed sites
danish_cover_or_density: Among the 3 most frequent algae on Danish boulder reefs at 10-22 m
gaps: Kelp density at nests not measured; R11 is a visual guess

name: Fucus spp. (bladder wrack, serrated wrack)
role_for_lumpfish: Juveniles in intertidal pools all summer, feeding on harpacticoid copepods 'characteristic of shoreline algae'; source of drift weed
danish_cover_or_density: Øresund 0-10 m (Oceana); no NOVANA value read
evidence: literature (direct for shoreline algae; species not named)
gaps: Which shoreline alga juveniles prefer is not named in readable sources

name: Red algae (Phycodrys rubens, Delesseria sanguinea, others)
role_for_lumpfish: Dominant cover on deeper boulder reefs (10-22 m); possible concealment for nests
needs: Stones; cover multi-layered at ~15 m, open deeper
danish_cover_or_density: Total macroalgal cover 2-80% at 15 ROV stations 10.5-22.5 m

name: Filamentous algae
role_for_lumpfish: Increase with depth and with eutrophication; can smother stones (nest quality risk, inferred)

name: Floating / drift seaweed
role_for_lumpfish: Young-of-year live near the surface 'attached to or under floating seaweed' (refuge and food)
needs: Attached algae upstream (F2, F3) to supply drift
gaps: Not designable directly; follows from attached algae

name: Wrasse (goldsinny Ctenolabrus rupestris, ballan, corkwing)
role_for_lumpfish: Cunner, a wrasse, ate eggs that guarding males could not defend (Newfoundland). Goldsinny is the most frequent fish on Danish boulder reefs, so a nest reef will attract likely egg predators
danish_cover_or_density: Most frequent fish at Danish boulder stations
gaps: No Danish data on wrasse eating lumpfish eggs

name: Cod, blennies
role_for_lumpfish: Eat submerged eggs (FAO synopsis, summary text)

name: Gulls, crows, rooks, starlings
role_for_lumpfish: Take intertidal eggs and guarding males; males 'particularly vulnerable to bird predation'
gaps: Matters only for very shallow nests (cf. Bembridge)

name: Seals (harbour, grey), otters
role_for_lumpfish: Take spawning adults close to shore; impact unknown
danish_cover_or_density: Harbour and grey seals common in Kattegat/Øresund

name: Harpacticoid copepods, amphipods, isopods
role_for_lumpfish: Juvenile food: harpacticoids on shoreline algae, then amphipods; also isopods, small fish larvae

name: Pelagic plankton, ctenophores, jellyfish
role_for_lumpfish: Adult food at sea; adults hardly feed when spawning (80% of 424 empty stomachs)

name: Sea urchins
role_for_lumpfish: Can graze down the whole algal community on Danish reefs, removing kelp cover

name: Starfish (Asterias rubens)
role_for_lumpfish: Common on Danish stones and sand; no source names it as an egg predator
gaps: In the Krea manifest but has no evidenced role; keep as background fauna only
